name: Alamedin Gorge
near: Koi-Tash is the last village on the approach to the gorge (on the Hiking.kg route: Kok-Jar → Besh-Kungei → Tash-Moinok → Koi-Tash); Bishkek is 30–35 km to the north (too.kg, Hiking.kg). “Tatyr 7.7 km” is a straight-line calculation, not an access route.
elev: The Teplye Klyuchi (Warm Springs) resort is at about 2,000 m (sxodim, 2022); the gain from the parking lot to the Teke-Tor waterfall is about 370 m (Hiking.kg), i.e. the waterfall is roughly ~2,300 m (calculation). Usechenko Peak above the gorge is 4,650 m (2GIS).
short: Alamedin is the mountain gorge closest to Bishkek (30–35 km), with the Teplye Klyuchi radon hot springs and the Teke-Tor waterfall.
desc: Alamedin is the mountain gorge of the Alamedin River on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Range, about 30 km south of Bishkek; it is called the gorge closest to the capital (too.kg). The paved road goes up to the Teplye Klyuchi resort — the only radon spring on the Kyrgyz Range: a 25 m pool, a mud-therapy clinic, water at 50–55 °C (too.kg, sxodim). From the end of the road it is about 5 km to the waterfall (Teke-Tor); farther up are the “Quiet Backwater” grove at the confluence of the Salyk stream and the Alamedin, Lake Altyn-Tor ~20 km away, and the Alamedin Pass into the Issyk-Ata gorge for the experienced (too.kg). The gorge has birch and juniper forests, berry meadows, and views of glaciers and Usechenko Peak (4,650 m); there are horseback rides, kymyz and a café (2GIS).
guide: Come in the morning: Hiking.kg warns that by evening the western slope shades the valley early. The classic is the 5.7 km trail to the Teke-Tor waterfall (about 2 h 10 min one way, gain ~370 m), and afterwards a hot radon pool at Teplye Klyuchi to loosen your legs. Drink water from springs, not from the river — livestock graze higher up the gorge (too.kg). The signal drops after about the 10th kilometer, at the resort, so an offline map does not hurt. If you want more, go to the “Quiet Backwater” grove by the Salyk stream, while the prepared continue to Lake Altyn-Tor (~20 km).
see: The Alamedin River, birch and juniper forests and meadows; the Teke-Tor waterfall (5.7 km from the parking lot); the radon springs and pool of Teplye Klyuchi; the “Quiet Backwater” grove by the Salyk stream; Lake Altyn-Tor (~20 km up the valley); views of the glaciers and Usechenko Peak, 4,650 m (too.kg, Hiking.kg, 2GIS).
skip: You are going on a weekend and dislike crowds — this is one of the most visited gorges near Bishkek (per video and 2GIS, 2,500+ ratings). You want wilderness without cafés and cottages — Kegety or Ala-Archa higher up the trails are better. You have already been to Ala-Archa and do not want hot springs — the scenery is similar.
diff: The approach is paved, easy. The trail to Teke-Tor: 2/5 on the Hiking.kg scale, 5.7 km one way, gain ~370 m; there is a steep section at the waterfall. The hike to Altyn-Tor and the Alamedin Pass are for the experienced (too.kg).
when: May–October for hiking (editorial: greenery, dry trails); the Teplye Klyuchi springs work year-round, and the road to the resort is paved. In winter the trail to the waterfall ices over — crampons/ice grips are needed (Hiking.kg).
hours: The gorge is open 24 hours; entry and parking are free (too.kg). The working hours of the Teplye Klyuchi resort and pool are not given on the pages — check by tel. +996 312 36-66-18, +996 773 48-58-80 (sxodim).
daytime: Early morning: in the evening the western slope shades the valley (Hiking.kg); also, before noon there are fewer people on the trail to the waterfall.
how: From Bishkek south along Shabdan Baatyr Avenue / via Kok-Jar, Besh-Kungei, Tash-Moinok and Koi-Tash to the start of the trail in the gorge — 35 km, about 1 h 10 min (Hiking.kg); paved to the Teplye Klyuchi resort (too.kg). Public transport does not run to the gorge — a taxi or a tour (sxodim).
needcar: Yes: a car, taxi or transfer to the parking lot at the resort; beyond that on foot. There is no public transport in the gorge (sxodim, 2022).
self: Yes: the road is paved, entry is free, the trail to Teke-Tor is simple (2/5) and popular (too.kg, Hiking.kg). For Altyn-Tor and the pass you need experience and equipment.
roadtype: Paved to the start of the walk / the Teplye Klyuchi resort (Hiking.kg, too.kg); beyond that — a footpath.
traveltime: Bishkek → parking lot: 35 km, ~1 h 10 min by car (Hiking.kg); on foot to Teke-Tor 5.7 km, ~2 h 10 min one way (Hiking.kg); the Sputnik8 tour — 1–1.5 h of driving one way.
stay: Teplye Klyuchi resort/recreation base: 9 three-block cottages, each block with 2 rooms with a shower and toilet (sxodim, 2022; prices by phone +996 312 36-66-18). Also the Jannat hotel, the “Koi-Tash” rest house, cottages at the resort, and summer bases with tapchans (raised platforms) (too.kg). Camping is deeper in the gorge, with few places by the road (too.kg). 2025–2026 prices were not found.
net: There is mobile coverage for the first ~10 km of the gorge — up to the Teplye Klyuchi resort; above it there is none (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
entry: Entry to the gorge and parking are free (too.kg). The pool/treatments at Teplye Klyuchi are paid, and the tariffs are not given on the pages (sxodim).
transfer: The Sputnik8 tour to the hot springs — $120 per group/excursion (5 h, transfer + guide; reviews 2023–2025). Taxi Bishkek – Alamedin: 2025–2026 prices were not found (Yandex Go/inDrive at the tariff).
bring: Trekking poles and non-slip shoes for the descents and the section by the waterfall; in winter — ice grips (Hiking.kg); swimwear for the springs; water or a filter (do not drink from the river — livestock), an offline map — the signal disappears above the resort (too.kg).
warn: Do not drink river water — livestock graze higher up (too.kg). The signal exists only up to the resort. The trail at the waterfall is steep and ices over in winter (Hiking.kg). Radon baths have contraindications — consult a doctor. The Alamedin Pass into Issyk-Ata is only for experienced groups (too.kg).
food: Kymyz and national cuisine at the local café (2GIS); the “12 Kaminov” (12 Fireplaces) café in the gorge (too.kg); berries and mushrooms in summer (2GIS) — pick only those you know.
reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 2,566 ratings (168 reviews) — as of 07.10.2026; Google Maps (the “Alamudun Gorge” listing): 4.9/5, 14 ratings — as of 03.10.2026; the Sputnik8 tour to the springs 4.7 (3 reviews). Pros: proximity to Bishkek, the waterfall, hot springs, nature; cons (per video/descriptions): crowded on weekends, cottage development by the road, the river water is not drinkable.
p.sum: The gorge closest to Bishkek (30–35 km, ~1 h): paved to the Teplye Klyuchi resort, free parking, then 5.5–5.7 km on foot to the Teke-Tor waterfall. Public transport does not run to the gorge — people go by taxi (Yandex Go one way; arrange waiting for the return), their own car, or with a tour ($90–190). An ideal day trip: the waterfall in the morning, then the radon pools and lunch at a café by the resort.

p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: the Teke-Tor waterfall, a night at Teplye Klyuchi or at a Koi-Tash hotel with springs. Day 2: a hike farther to the “Quiet Backwater” grove/toward Altyn-Tor, or a horseback ride.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: The neighboring gorges of the Kyrgyz Range — Chunkurchak (skiing/horses), Ala-Archa (through the city). In summer experienced groups — the Alamedin Pass into Issyk-Ata.
p.season: May–October — the best for hiking; June–July — greenery, kymyz, many people on weekends; the springs work year-round, the road is paved; November–March — the trail to the waterfall ices over, ice grips are needed (Hiking.kg).
p.budget.economy: A taxi Bishkek – Teplye Klyuchi round trip (Yandex tariff, not confirmed) split among 3–4 people; entry and parking 0; food at a café ~500–800 som; in total a guideline of 1,000–2,000 som/person (estimate)
p.budget.comfort: The Sputnik8 tour $90 (1–3 people) – $130; or kg.country $190/person; + thermal treatments/lunch; a night at Mountain View ~$145
p.permits: Not needed. Entry to the gorge and parking are free (too.kg).
p.access: Excellent with children: paved to the resort, pools; the trail to the waterfall for children 7+ (kg.country), with a steep final section. For older people — the resort and short walks; with a stroller — only the resort/hotel grounds. With a dog — the trail yes, at the resorts check.
